tips.title: Le, la, les — before the verb
tips.body: *Je regarde la série* → *je **la** regarde.* The pronoun replaces the noun and moves **in front of the verb**. *Le* for a masculine noun, *la* for feminine, *les* for any plural; *l'* before a vowel. English puts *it* after; French puts it before.

tips.title: Me, te, nous, vous too
tips.body: *Il m'écoute* (he listens to me), *je t'aime, elle **nous** invite, je **vous** comprends.* The same slot holds *me, te, nous, vous* — the same forms as the reflexive pronouns, and in the same place.

tips.title: The negative wraps pronoun and verb
tips.body: *Je **ne le** regarde **pas**.* *Ne* goes before the pronoun, *pas* after the verb, and the pronoun stays glued to its verb — exactly like a reflexive.

tips.title: With an infinitive, before the infinitive
tips.body: *Je vais **la** voir demain. Je veux **les** acheter. Je peux t'aider.* When the verb you mean is an infinitive, the pronoun sits in front of it, not in front of *vais / veux / peux*.

tips.title: In the perfect, before avoir — and the participle agrees
tips.body: *J'ai vu la série* → *je **l'ai vue***. The pronoun goes before *ai*, and because the direct object now comes **before** the participle, the participle **agrees** with it: *vue* for *la série*, *achetés* for *les billets*. After *avoir*, the participle agrees only with a direct object placed before it; a pronoun is the commonest case (you will also meet *la série que j'ai vue*).

why.matters: *Do you like football? Yes, I love it.* The *it* is a direct object pronoun, and French puts it before the verb, where English never does: *je l'adore*. The topic exists because repeating a noun reads as clumsy in any language, because the reading paper uses *le, la, les* to point back at nouns and expects you to follow, and because the pronoun's position is one of the clearest signs of a student who thinks in French. It also opens the door to the agreement that lifts a perfect tense into the top band: *je l'ai vue*.

examples.title: Tu aimes le foot ? Oui, je l'adore
examples.body: A conversation runs on pronouns, because nobody repeats the noun. *Tu regardes la série ? Oui, je la regarde tous les soirs. Tu as les billets ? Oui, je les ai.* The pronoun takes the gender and number of the noun it replaces, and it goes in front of the verb, so the French sentence sounds back to front to an English ear until it stops sounding that way. People are replaced the same way: *je vois mon frère* becomes *je le vois*.

examples.title: Four positions, one rule
examples.body: The pronoun sits in front of the verb it belongs to, and that single rule settles four cases that look different: the plain present, *je la regarde*; the negative, *je ne la regarde pas*, with the pronoun inside the *ne … pas*; the infinitive, *je vais la regarder*, where the pronoun goes before the second verb because that is the verb it belongs to; and the perfect, *je l'ai regardée*, before the auxiliary. Learn it as one rule and the four cases stop being four.

examples.title: The participle that agrees
examples.body: In the perfect tense with *avoir*, the participle normally stays put: *j'ai vu ma sœur*. Put the object in front as a pronoun and the participle agrees with it: *je l'ai vue*, with an *e* for the sister. Nobody hears it, but a reader sees it in writing, because it shows that the writer knows which noun the pronoun stands for. It is the single most reliable marker of control in a Year 9 perfect tense, and it costs one letter.

steps.title: Le, la, les
steps.body: A **direct object pronoun** replaces the thing or person a verb acts on, so you do not repeat the noun. *Tu aimes **le foot** ?* — *Oui, je l'adore.* *Tu regardes **la série** ?* — *Oui, je **la** regarde tous les soirs.* *Tu as **les billets** ?* — *Oui, je **les** ai.* **The forms**: **le** (him, it — masculine), **la** (her, it — feminine), **les** (them), and l' for *le / la* before a vowel or silent *h*. On the Pearson specification, *les* meaning *them* is on the Higher-tier vocabulary list, as is *leur*; Foundation papers use *le, la, l'* and *me, te, nous, vous*. **The position**: **before the verb**. *Je le regarde, elle les achète, nous l'écoutons.* Never after, as in English. **People too**: *je vois **mon frère** tous les jours* → *je **le** vois tous les jours*. *J'invite **mes amies*** → *je **les** invite*. **Me, te, nous, vous** fill the same slot: *il **me** regarde, je t'écoute, elle **nous** attend* (waits for us), *je **vous** comprends*. **Only for direct objects** — verbs with no preposition: *regarder, aimer, voir, acheter, écouter* (no *à* in French!), *attendre, chercher, inviter, comprendre, connaître, prendre*.

check.solution: **Je la regarde.** *La télé* is feminine singular.

steps.title: Négatifs, infinitifs et le passé composé
steps.body: **Negative**: *ne* goes before the pronoun, *pas* after the verb — *je **ne** le regarde **pas***, *elle **ne** m'écoute **jamais***. The pronoun never separates from its verb. **With an infinitive** — after *aller, vouloir, pouvoir, devoir, aimer*: the pronoun goes **before the infinitive**: *je vais **la** voir demain*, *je veux **les** acheter*, *tu peux m'aider ?*, *je dois **le** finir*. Not *je la vais voir*. **In the perfect tense**: the pronoun goes **before the auxiliary**: *je l'ai vu, elle **les** a achetés, nous t'avons attendu*. Negative: *je **ne** l'ai **pas** vu*. **Agreement in the perfect**: when the direct object comes **before** the participle — which a pronoun always does — the participle **agrees** with it: - *J'ai vu **le film*** → *je l'ai **vu*** (masculine, no change) - *J'ai vu **la série*** → *je l'ai **vue*** - *J'ai acheté **les billets*** → *je les ai **achetés*** - *J'ai invité **mes amies*** → *je les ai **invitées*** **Questions**: *Tu l'as vu ? Est-ce que tu les connais ?* — the pronoun stays before the verb. **With voici / voilà**: *le voici* (here he is), *les voilà* (there they are).

steps.title: Quand utiliser les pronoms
steps.body: **Why use them**: a text or speaking answer that repeats *la série, la série, la série* sounds like a beginner. A pronoun in the second sentence sounds like French. **Where they appear in exam texts**: *je l'ai acheté* (I bought it), *on les a invités* (we invited them), *tu peux m'aider ?*, *je ne les comprends pas* (I do not understand them), *il m'énerve* (he annoys me), *ça m'intéresse* (that interests me), *je t'adore*. **Working out what le / la / les refers to**: find the noun in the previous sentence that matches in gender and number. *J'ai un nouveau portable. Je l'adore.* — *l'* = *le portable*. **Do not confuse with the article**: *je regarde **la** télé* (article — the) vs *je **la** regarde* (pronoun — it). Same word, different job: the article stands before a noun, the pronoun before a verb. **Indirect objects are different**: verbs with *à* — *parler à, téléphoner à, donner à, faire confiance à* — take *lui / leur*, not *le / la / les*: *je **lui** parle* (I speak to him / her), *je **leur** téléphone* (I phone them). If the French verb has *à* before the person, the pronoun is *lui / leur*. **Counting with pronouns**: *j'ai regardé 4 épisodes et il **en** reste 6* — 10 in all. (*En* = of them — a pronoun for a later topic.)

steps.title: Your turn
steps.body:
**Part A.**

1. Replace the noun: *je regarde le film, je mange la pizza, j'achète les billets*.
2. Write *he listens to me* and *I understand you* (tu).
3. Write *I love it* about a feminine noun starting with a vowel — which pronoun?

**Part B.**

4. Make negative: *je le regarde, je les invite*.
5. Write *I want to buy them* and *can you help me?*
6. Put in the perfect with a pronoun: *j'ai vu la série, j'ai acheté les chaussures*.

**Part C.**

7. Explain why *je l'ai vue* has an *-e* but *j'ai vu la série* does not.
8. Write one sentence with *lui* and one with *le / la* and explain the choice.
9. Write a short conversation of five lines about a film, using a pronoun in every reply.

For question 9, every pronoun sits before the verb it belongs to.

steps.title: Going deeper
steps.body:
**Before the verb, always.** *Je la regarde, je ne la regarde pas, je vais la regarder, je l'ai regardée.* Four positions, one rule: in front of the verb it belongs to.

**Elide.** *Je l'adore, il m'attend, je t'écoute.* Writing *je le adore* is as visible as *je me habille*.

**Agree the participle after a preceding object.** *Je l'ai vue, je les ai achetés, on les a invitées.* This rule is on both tiers of the specification, and it is mechanical: find the object, check its gender and number, add *-e / -s / -es*.

**Direct or indirect?** No *à* → *le / la / les*; *à* → *lui / leur*. *Je la vois* but *je lui parle*. English cannot help you here — *listen to* is *écouter* with no *à*, *phone* is *téléphoner à* with one.

**Read for the referent.** In a text, *l'* or *les* points back to a noun of matching gender and number. Find it, and the sentence makes sense.

**Use pronouns to avoid repetition.** *J'ai acheté un nouveau jeu. Je l'adore et je le trouve passionnant.* Two pronouns in the second sentence is native-sounding French.

**Combine with the reflexive slot.** *Je me lève* and *je le lave* use the same position — the pronoun before the verb — and mastering one is mastering the other.

**Pronouns in questions and answers.** *Tu les as vus ?* — *Oui, je les ai vus.* Reusing the pronoun in the reply is the speaking-exam pattern.

props.title: The sixth row is the rule that lifts the band

visuals.alt: A table of common errors with direct object pronouns and the correct forms

steps.title: Summary
steps.body: - **Direct object pronouns**: *me, te, le, la, nous, vous, les*; *m', t', l'* before a vowel. - *Le* = him / it (m), *la* = her / it (f), *les* = them. - **Position: before the verb**: *je la regarde*. - **Negative**: *je **ne** la regarde **pas***. - **Infinitive**: *je vais **la** voir, je veux **les** acheter, tu peux m'aider ?* - **Perfect**: before *avoir* — *je l'ai vu*; negative *je **ne** l'ai **pas** vu*. - **Agreement**: the participle agrees with a **preceding** direct object — *je l'ai vu**e***, *je les ai acheté**s***. - Direct verbs: *regarder, écouter, attendre, chercher, voir, aimer, connaître, aider, inviter, comprendre*. - **À** → indirect: *parler à, téléphoner à, donner à* take **lui / leur**. - Article vs pronoun: *je regarde **la** télé* / *je **la** regarde*. - In a text, *l' / les* points back to the matching noun. - *Le voici, les voilà.*

visuals.alt: A summary table of direct object pronouns and their positions

questions.prompt: Why does **je l'ai vue** take an *-e* when **j'ai vu la série** does not?
options: Vue is the feminine form used after any pronoun
The participle agrees with a direct object that comes before it
Verbs with avoir always agree with the subject when the subject is feminine
The -e marks that the action is finished
questions.solution: After *avoir*, the participle agrees only when the direct object **precedes** it. A pronoun always does, so *je l'ai **vue*** (*la série*); with the noun after the verb there is no agreement.

questions.prompt: Translate into English: **je ne les ai pas invités parce qu'ils m'énervent**.
options: I didn't invite them because they annoy me.
They didn't invite me because I annoy them.
I invited them because they annoy me.
I didn't invite them because they make me nervous.
questions.solution: **I didn't invite them because they annoy me.** *Ne … pas* wraps *ai*, so dropping it gives "I invited them"; *je* is the subject and *les* the object, so "they didn't invite me" swaps them; *énerver* means to annoy, not to make nervous. *Invités* agrees with the preceding *les*.

options: Je les ai vu hier et je les vais revoir demain.
J'ai les vus hier et je vais revoir les demain.
Je les ai vus hier et je vais revoir les demain.
Je les ai vus hier et je vais les revoir demain.

questions.prompt: Write a conversation of about 80 words in French between two friends about a series or a film. Use pronouns (le, la, les, l') instead of repeating the nouns: · in the present · in the negative · with an infinitive · in the perfect tense.
questions.solution:
— Tu regardes la nouvelle série sur Netflix ?
— Oui, je la regarde tous les soirs. Je l'adore !
— Tu as vu le dernier épisode ?
— Non, je ne l'ai pas encore vu. Je vais le regarder ce soir.
— Et l'actrice principale, tu la connais ?
— Oui, je l'ai vue dans un film l'année dernière. Elle est géniale.
— Mes cousins veulent la voir aussi. Je vais leur envoyer le lien.
— Bonne idée. Tu peux m'aider à trouver la deuxième saison ?
— Bien sûr, je la cherche et je t'envoie le lien.

examTechnique.body:
A direct object pronoun goes **before the verb** it belongs to — before the main verb, before the infinitive, before *avoir* in the perfect — and elides before a vowel. *Ne … pas* wraps pronoun and verb together.

For the top band, agree the participle with a preceding direct object (*je l'ai vue*) and choose *lui / leur* when the French verb takes *à*.
examinerErrors: No agreement in je les ai achetées.
Je le parle for je lui parle.
Repeating the noun instead of using a pronoun.
examTechnique.grade9Looks: A grade 9 answer places every pronoun before its verb in all four positions, elides it before vowels, and wraps the negative round the pair. It agrees the participle with a preceding direct object without hesitation, distinguishes *le / la / les* from *lui / leur* by whether the French verb takes *à*, and uses pronouns to avoid repetition so the French reads naturally.
